title: Epidemiology and Management of Early Blight (Alternaria solani) in Tomato Crops
summary: Field trials verify that relative humidity exceeding 80% for >8 continuous hours and temperatures between 24-30C stimulate massive Alternaria solani sporulation. Copper hydroxide spray shows 88% prophylactic efficacy when applied before canopy closure.

title: Comparative Study on Biological vs Chemical Control for Solanaceous Blights
summary: Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide establishes competitive exclusion on leaf phyllosphere, suppressing Early Blight progression with 78% protection rating without synthetic residues.

title: Organic Farming Advisory: Neem Oil Efficacy in Fungal Control
summary: Recommends neem oil 2% extract as fully effective preventative and curative spray against Early Blight and Powdery Mildew in tomato fields.

title: Comprehensive Systematic Review on Botanical Fungicides in Open Field Agriculture
summary: Rigorous multi-site randomized trials establish that Neem Oil Extract is INSUFFICIENT as a standalone curative treatment against established Early Blight (Alternaria solani) infections and can result in severe defoliation if relied upon under high humidity (>85%).

title: Soil Physical-Chemical Characteristics and Vegetable Root Disease Vulnerability
summary: Poorly drained heavy clay soils with pH < 5.8 create root hypoxia, elevating tomato vulnerability to soil-borne fungi and bacterial wilts.

title: Automated Agro-Meteorological Station Telemetry Feed - Station South-East Valley
summary: Live telemetry providing calibrated calibrated hourly ambient temperature, leaf moisture, and relative humidity recordings.

title: District Farmer Diagnostic Advisory Field Note: Tomato Blight Cluster
summary: Farmer field inspectors reported 35% foliar target-ring lesion symptoms across 14 tomato plots following 4 days of continuous overcast drizzle and night humidity > 90%.
